conviction_note: abs_move 14 (implied 13.1%, first combined guide after the LivePerson close, 42% of float short) times a mild long lean (p_up 56): the headline revenue bar most wires carry ($61.7-63.0M) excludes 27 days of LivePerson, the deal brought ~$97M of cash, and the short is crowded into a 52-week low. Against that, LivePerson is shrinking and a new ex-LivePerson CFO sets the first combined guide. The findings sum to +1.20 and the scaled number is +1.68. They roughly agree; the gap is the extra weight p_up gives to the crowded short and to the first-guide magnitude.
bar: Disputed. Most-cited Q3 revenue consensus: $61.71M from TipRanks (https://www.tipranks.com/news/soundhound-ai-q3-earnings-today-wall-street-and-options-markets-last-minute-verdict-on-soun-stock, 2026-11-05), $62.8M from Benzinga (cited at https://financefeeds.com/soun-stock-falls-3-7-ahead-of-q3-earnings-tonight/, 2026-11-05) and ~$63.0M from Zacks. These look standalone or near-standalone: $61.7M is +46.9% y/y on $42.0M and flat on Q2's $61.9M. The LivePerson-inclusive consensus is ~$77.2M (Motley Fool via https://tech-insider.org/ca/?p=3026, 2026-11-01), one source only. I size print_vs_bar against the $77.2M LP-inclusive bar, which I take as the informed bar. EPS bar also disputed: TipRanks -$0.13 (GAAP-like), Zacks adjusted -$0.06. No company Q3 guide; FY26 guide $230-260M excludes LivePerson (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001840856/000184085626000019/soun-20260806ex991earnings.htm). Because the bar is disputed, findings that depend on it are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 170,799,103 shares = 41.87% of float, 10.05 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15, up 7.47% from 2026-09-30 (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/SoundHound+AI+Stock+Short+Interest+Rises+to+41.87%25, published 2026-10-29). Sealed baseline: 25d skew -29.29 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.17, ATM IV 223%, straddle 13.14%, spot $4.07 at the 52-week low, -26.3% over 20 days, -74% from the 52-week high. Crowded short plus call-side skew: the option market leans up and a squeeze is a live mechanism. 36.9M shares issued to LivePerson noteholders carry a resale shelf (8-K 2026-09-04).

findings.finding: The widely carried Q3 revenue consensus ($61.71M TipRanks, $62.8M Benzinga, ~$63.0M Zacks) looks like SoundHound standalone: $61.7M is +46.9% y/y and flat on Q2's $61.9M. Reported Q3 revenue will include 27 days of LivePerson, closed 2026-09-04. At LivePerson's last Q3 consensus of $49.1M a quarter, that is roughly $12-15M before any deferred-revenue haircut. Reported revenue near $75-80M would therefore print as a ~20%+ 'beat' against the headline bar, while landing only ~in line with the LP-inclusive $77.2M bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought and sold: Q2 2026 beat ($61.9M vs ~$52.5M est., adj EPS -$0.02 vs -$0.13) went +10.1%; Q3 2025 beat and raise went -0.6%; Q1 2026 (+52% revenue, margin compression) went -7.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Informed holders know LP is in the quarter; the Motley Fool $77.2M figure shows some analysts updated. But the wires and the day-of previews (TipRanks, Benzinga, financefeeds) all carry the ~$62M figure, so headline and algorithmic readers will see a large 'beat'. If the market had fully absorbed this, previews would quote an LP-inclusive number and the headline consensus would sit near $75M.
findings.independence: Bar dispute documented at https://tech-insider.org/ca/?p=3026 (2026-11-01, 'some trackers still show a stale ~$61.7M') and at https://financefeeds.com/soun-stock-falls-3-7-ahead-of-q3-earnings-tonight/ (2026-11-05). LP Q3 run-rate from LPSN consensus $49.1M (Benzinga LPSN forecasts page, snippet_only). The close date and the 27 days come from the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1840856/000121390026097712/ea0304691-8k_sound.htm.

findings.finding: LivePerson brought cash onto SoundHound's balance sheet: $96.7M at 2026-06-30, with H1 2026 operating cash flow of +$10.8M. At close SoundHound paid only $5.85M cash to LP's secured noteholders, plus cash for TASE shares at $3.31 each. Combined Q3-end cash should therefore sit well above SoundHound's standalone path of ~$203M less ~$30M a quarter of burn. That eases the dilution and ATM fear (third ATM agreement dated 2026-05-11) that has weighed on the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash burn and dilution have been the sell-side complaint: FCF missed estimates four quarters running (Q2 -$34.1M vs -$23.8M est., per TIKR 2026-10-20). No clean prior reaction to a cash surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage frames the deal as dilution and integration risk (TIKR, Ives) and quotes SoundHound's standalone $203M. No preview found adds LP's cash or its cash-flow-positive H1. If this were priced, previews would quote a pro-forma cash figure and the burn narrative would not be the lead bear point.
findings.independence: Payments to noteholders come from SoundHound's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1840856/000121390026097712/ea0304691-8k_sound.htm). SoundHound's standalone cash and the ATM come from its 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001840856/000184085626000022/soun-20260630.htm). LP's $15M of 2026 notes and transaction costs reduce the net amount; still clearly positive.

findings.finding: The company promised a guidance update after the LivePerson close, so the first combined outlook is due tonight. LP's revenue is shrinking: Q2 2026 $52.5M (-11.9% y/y), Americas $26.4M vs $38.1M, and current deferred revenue down from $54.3M to $46.2M on 'changes in customer renewal patterns'. Management's earlier 2027 framework was $350-400M including ≥$100M from LP customers, while FY27 consensus sits near ~$390M at the top of that range. A combined guide that merely reiterates the framework would land below the Street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises have been bought (Q2 2026 raise to $230-260M: +10.1%; Feb 2025: +17.5%) but not always (Nov 2025 raise: -0.6%). There is no prior combined-company guide.
findings.why_not_priced: FY27 consensus near $390M (TIKR 2026-10-20) sits near the top of the $350-400M framework, which shows the Street has not marked down for LP's attrition and deferred-revenue decline. Purchase accounting will also cut recognized LP deferred revenue. If priced, FY27 estimates would sit near the framework midpoint.
findings.independence: The $350-400M framework incl. ≥$100M LP is at https://www.itiger.com/news/1138887645 (2026-04-30). FY27 ~$390M consensus is at https://www.tikr.com/blog/soundhound-ai-just-dropped-21-in-a-month-is-it-time-to-sell-or-load-up (2026-10-20). Promise to update guidance: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001840856/000184085626000019/soun-20260806ex991earnings.htm. Net of the rest: SoundHound standalone is ~75-80% of combined and grew 45% in Q2. If the standalone guide is raised, the LP drag can be offset, hence the wide band.

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded short into the print: 170.8M shares short, 41.87% of float, 10.05 days to cover as of 2026-10-15, up 7.5% from 2026-09-30. The stock sits at its 52-week low ($4.07, -26% in 20 days) and the options pay up for calls (25d skew -29 vol points, put/call OI 0.17). Any non-negative guide gives shorts a reason to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The upside reactions in the baseline are large (+26.4%, +17.5%, +10.1%) and the downside ones moderate (-7.8%, -7.8%, -4.2%, -0.6%). That skew of outcomes is consistent with short covering on non-bad prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: call skew already says upside is paid. What the price shows is a 26% slide into the print, so the shorts have not been squeezed beforehand.
findings.independence: Skew and put/call come from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options) and the run-up from the baseline tape; they share no source with the short interest figure.

findings.finding: SoundHound closed an acquisition on 2026-05-12: a membership-interest purchase, up to $30.2M cash, $28.0M allocated to customer relationships. It contributed only about seven weeks to Q2 and contributes a full quarter to Q3. Colombia revenue rose to $7.6M in Q2 2026 from $0.1M a year earlier. Together these support standalone sequential growth above the flat ~$62M implied by the headline consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as revenue line above: mixed, Q2 beat +10.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in the 10-Q notes, not in any preview. The headline consensus being flat sequentially suggests models did not pick up the full-quarter effect. The link between the Colombia revenue and the acquisition is my inference, not stated.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q document only; it shares the revenue line with finding 1 but rests on a different fact (the standalone base, not LP).

findings.finding: SoundHound's CFO is now John D. Collins, LivePerson's CFO/COO since 2020, appointed at close on 2026-09-04 (the Q2 release quoted an interim CFO). Tonight is his first SoundHound call and first combined guide. A new CFO setting a first outlook tends toward conservatism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior SoundHound print under a newly appointed CFO in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 8-K but absent from previews. The conservatism effect is inference, not documented.
findings.independence: None; behavioural inference from the 8-K only.

findings.finding: Resale overhang: 36,894,839 SoundHound shares (~8% of pre-deal count) were issued to LivePerson's first- and second-lien noteholders, with registration rights and a resale prospectus (424B7) filed 2026-09-04. LP shareholders also received 0.4673 SOUN per share. Sellers of this stock can lean on any post-print rally.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 20-day run-up of -26% after the close is consistent with the overhang being worked off, but it is not proven.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. TIKR (2026-10-20) attributes the fall to share-count growth. What is not visible is how much of the 36.9M has already been sold.
findings.independence: https://www.tikr.com/blog/soundhound-ai-just-dropped-21-in-a-month-is-it-time-to-sell-or-load-up (2026-10-20) names the share count as the cause of the slide.

findings.finding: Five9, a contact-center AI peer and LivePerson-adjacent counterparty, reported on 2026-08-06, after SoundHound's 2026-08-05 print. Its AI revenue was ~$39M (+78% y/y) and it raised its FY AI revenue growth outlook to ≥60% from >40%. This points to enterprise voice and agent AI demand strong into H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured SoundHound reaction to peer reads.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy only. It is three months old and Five9's Q3 2026 print was not found. If it were relevant and priced, SOUN would not have diverged from software peers (Trefis notes Five9 rose while SOUN fell).
findings.independence: Proxy; https://www.trefis.com/stock/soun/articles/619363/what-just-happened-to-soundhound-ai-stock/2026-10-20 notes the sector was not marked down.

findings.finding: Shareholder-law-firm investigations of officers and directors (Kahn Swick & Foti, Kuehn Law, Halper Sadeh) tie back to a federal securities suit over material weaknesses in internal controls. A notice landed on 2026-10-12, the day the stock fell 7.8% with no company news. If the 10-Q again reports an unremediated material weakness, or the merger adds one, it reinforces the governance discount.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Oct 12 -7.8% day coincided with a law-firm notice; causality unproven.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Law-firm notices are recurring since 2025. Only a new control disclosure in the 10-Q would add information.
findings.independence: Kuehn Law notice on the material-weakness suit: https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/246937/Kuehn-Law-Encourages-Investors-of-SoundHound-AI-Inc.-to-Contact-Law-Firm (May 2026).

findings.finding: GAAP EPS will carry LivePerson merger and transaction costs plus new intangible amortization in Q3. Against a GAAP-like -$0.13 bar (TipRanks), a GAAP miss is likely even if adjusted EPS (Zacks -$0.06 bar) is in line. Q2 2026 GAAP EPS was -$0.10 against non-GAAP -$0.02.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SoundHound trades on revenue and guidance; GAAP losses have been large every quarter without being the reaction driver.
findings.why_not_priced: One-off below operating line with no path to guidance; sized at a fraction. Headline 'misses EPS' risk only.
findings.independence: Q2 GAAP and non-GAAP EPS come from the company release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001840856/000184085626000019/soun-20260806ex991earnings.htm

baseline_tension: Agrees with the call-bid skew (-29 vol points) and with the crowded short, and cuts against the -26% 20-day run-up. Agreeing with the skew means part of the long lean is already in option prices, so p_up is held near 56 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): the headline-beat finding rests on a disputed bar (three agreeing ~$62M sources against a single-source $77.2M), so it was capped from +1.5 to +1.0, and p_up moved 57 to 56.
Rule 7 / lesson table (sign agrees with a strong skew, so partly priced): the positioning finding was cut from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 2 (one-offs below operating income): the GAAP EPS merger-cost finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.2.

Left standing: LP cash (rule 4: the financing question was answered, the money is cash on hand, not a raise), the guidance finding net of the standalone business (rule 9), the CFO and overhang findings, and the proxies sized small (rule 5).
